source.network: Al Jazeera English (aljazeera.com, News — staff with AFP and Reuters)
source.title: Saudi Arabia reports new attack on key East-West pipeline
source.byline: Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters
source.note: published 11-09 22:10 UTC; the 11-09 sweep matched it on 'diesel' (strait of) alone. Read in full on 11-10 via the cloud fetch (complete, 8 body paragraphs) as paragraph reductions, no quotation over ten words. A wire-form page — no reader voices; the Saudi energy ministry via SPA is the one party quoted. Cut 11-10 from the 11-09 sweep (no 11-10 sweep on GitHub at run time) as the LI corner's newest full-text row on the live object: the gate's bypass, attacked — the newest-first rule; the AJ newsfeed video on the Qatari prime minister's visit (18:48 UTC) left, the same meeting being on the Fox page cut today

object.label: H6 — the gate (PG01, proposed 10-15: US control of the Strait of Hormuz), read from the LI corner outside the US horizon six days after the vote, from its far side: the route around it. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline — 1,200 km across the peninsula to Yanbu, carrying about 4 million barrels a day rerouted since the Strait was constricted, about 4 percent of global supply — attacked again on Monday in the Medina region; a 'limited fire', no casualties, operations not affected (the energy ministry via SPA); no attacker named, with the Houthi war intensifying beneath it and the September shutdown (drones from Iraq) as the precedent. The page's frame is the publication's own: the Strait 'tightly constricted by the US-Israel war on Iran', the war fuelling 'a global energy crisis'. The holder, the talks, the pump and the vote are not on the page; the gate is there as the thing the pipeline exists to bypass

zAxis.pos: the gate holds and the war closes on US terms — the Strait reopens and the bypass becomes redundancy
zAxis.neg: it does not — the Strait stays constricted, the bypass becomes the route, and the route itself becomes a theatre

object.gear: the barrel (the route, the throughput, the share of supply) and the war itself (the theatre widened to the bypass); nothing on the pump, the vote or the dollar

transformNote: no promise and no holder on the page. What the page does to the object is read the gate from its far side: the bypass that exists because the gate is shut is now itself under attack, for at least the third time (September, shut for days; 'several times'; Monday). The shadow has no form here — the page names no one for the Monday attack and sizes it small by the party that owns the pipe. The publication's one frame is the war's name ('US-Israel war on Iran') and its effect ('a global energy crisis'), the house term on every Al Jazeera page since 10-21

lines.quote: 'new attack on key East-West pipeline'; 'essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz'
lines.note: THE DOOR (hed + dek) — the bypass attacked; the gate in the dek as the thing bypassed
lines.zWhy: a bypass under attack reads the gate as still shut and the route as the next theatre

lines.quote: the pipeline hit by 'another' attack, per state media
lines.note: the record — the one word that dates it ('another')
lines.zWhy: a pipeline hit again is a war that has reached the route around the gate

lines.quote: targeted Monday in the Medina region; a 'limited fire', extinguished; no injuries or deaths; operations not affected
lines.note: THE PARTY'S COUNT — the attack sized small by the state that owns the pipe (¶2–3 folded; SPA the channel)
lines.zWhy: a fire put out with operations unaffected is a bypass holding, for now

lines.quote: no attacker named; fighting intensifying between Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government coalition it backs, and the Iran-backed Houthis
lines.note: THE THEATRE — the attack left unaddressed and set inside the Yemen war; later sighting of the war's other front (nyt 11-08 'More Than 50 Killed in Yemen'; aj 11-09 'Yemen government forces claim new advances', both uncut)
lines.zWhy: a route attacked from a widening war is a gate whose closing has opened a second front

lines.quote: the Strait 'tightly constricted by the US-Israel war on Iran'; attacked several times 'as the war on Iran fuels a global energy crisis'
lines.note: THE FRAME — the publication's house term for the war and its effect; the page's ceiling
lines.zWhy: a Strait constricted by a war that fuels a crisis is a gate the war has not closed on anyone's terms

lines.quote: the Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi oil infrastructure — refineries, storage — with drones and missiles
lines.note: the pattern — the bypass's attackers by precedent, unnamed for Monday
lines.zWhy: infrastructure repeatedly targeted is a route priced as a target

lines.quote: 1,200 km across the peninsula; shut for several days in September after drone attacks Saudi Arabia said were launched from Iraq
lines.note: THE PIPELINE SIZED, THE PRECEDENT DATED — the September shutdown the one time the bypass failed
lines.zWhy: a bypass that has already been shut once is a route that can be closed

lines.quote: about 4 million barrels a day rerouted via the pipeline to Yanbu since the Strait was disrupted — about 4 percent of global supply
lines.note: THE BYPASS SIZED — the floor; the barrel's route around the gate counted; the number the Fox page's 4.4 million (the UAE, Fujairah) sits beside
lines.zWhy: four percent of the world's barrel going around the gate is a gate the barrel has learned to avoid
